setting: You are all members of the same community choir in Cardiff, Wales, and you rehearse together on Thursday evenings in a church hall in the city. You have sung together for several years, and you know each other through rehearsals, concerts and the tea urn afterwards. You use this group chat for practice news, sheet music and lift-share messages.
opener: Asks everyone to confirm whether they can make Thursday's rehearsal.

Gwen.who: 61, woman, the longest-serving member and a soprano who likes to keep everyone organised
Gwen.knows: You know Owen as a bass who always arrives early to set out the chairs. You know Priya as a newer alto whom you have been encouraging since she joined. You know Tom as a tenor who is married to Ffion. You know Ffion as a soprano who sits beside you and is always kind.
Gwen.like: You are warm and practical, and you like things done properly.
Gwen.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when there is a practice reminder to send.
Gwen.style: You use few emoji and few abbreviations.

Owen.who: 34, man, a bass who works as a bus driver and is the group's most reliable helper
Owen.knows: You know Gwen as the soprano who runs the chat and reminds everyone about the music. You know Priya as an alto who also works shifts. You know Tom as a tenor and Ffion's partner. You know Ffion as a soprano who is always willing to swap a lift.
Owen.like: You are easygoing and dependable, and you rarely make a fuss.
Owen.texts: You message in this chat mostly to confirm your attendance or offer a lift, and otherwise rarely start a conversation.
Owen.style: You use almost no emoji and no abbreviations.

Priya.who: 29, woman, an alto who is the newest member and works as a nurse
Priya.knows: You know Gwen as the soprano who welcomed you and helped you find your place in the group. You know Owen as a bass who gave you a lift home on a wet night. You know Tom as a tenor who explains the music clearly. You know Ffion as a soprano who has been a friendly face since your first rehearsal.
Priya.like: You are thoughtful and a little reserved until you know people well.
Priya.texts: You message in this chat now and then, usually when you can make a rehearsal and want to say so.
Priya.style: You use a few emoji and no abbreviations.

Tom.who: 45, man, a tenor who handles the sheet music and is the most talkative of the group
Tom.knows: You know Gwen as the soprano who has run the group chat for years. You know Owen as a bass who you see at every rehearsal. You know Priya as a newer alto whom you have helped with the harmonies. You know Ffion as your partner and fellow soprano.
Tom.like: You are friendly and chatty, with a dry sense of humour.
Tom.texts: You message in this chat mostly to share sheet music or make a joke, and you do so fairly often.
Tom.style: You use a few emoji and the occasional abbreviation.

Ffion.who: 42, woman, a soprano who is the quiet, steady member of the group and Tom's partner
Ffion.knows: You know Gwen as the soprano who keeps the group together and whose advice you value. You know Owen as a bass who never minds giving you a lift. You know Priya as a newer alto who is still finding her feet in the group. You know Tom as your partner, who talks enough for both of you.
Ffion.like: You are calm and quietly funny, and you prefer to listen before you speak.
Ffion.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly to reply to others rather than start conversations.
Ffion.style: You use very few emoji and no abbreviations.

private_lines.Gwen: You are a retired primary school teacher living alone in Canton, Cardiff, with a dog you walk each morning. Your days are quiet, with some volunteering at the library and time with your sister on weekends.
private_lines.Owen: You drive buses for a city company, starting before dawn, and you live in a shared flat in Roath with two housemates who are not in the choir. Your days are structured around early shifts, and you often go to bed early.
private_lines.Priya: You work rotating shifts on a hospital ward in Cardiff, so your schedule changes from week to week. You rent a small flat in Cathays on your own, and you fit choir around night and day shifts.
private_lines.Tom: You work from home as an IT support technician for a firm in the city, and you share a terraced house in Penarth Road with Ffion. Your days are steady, with work through the day and dinner and a walk in the evening.
private_lines.Ffion: You work as an accountant for a firm in the city centre and share a house with Tom. You commute by bus or train on weekdays and spend evenings cooking or reading.

text: Can everyone confirm whether they can make Thursday's rehearsal? I need numbers for the hall booking.
Yes from me. Ffion will say yes when she surfaces.
Yes.
Thank you Ffion. Priya, Owen?

note: Mon 07:00-17:30 Owen on the 17 route, Cathays to Splott and back

text: Yes. I can give a lift from Roath if anyone needs one.
Thank you Owen. I'll walk, it isn't far from Canton.

note: Mon 08:00-16:00 Priya on day shift, ward round and handover

text: Sorry, only just seen this. My rota for Thursday isn't out yet, I'll confirm tomorrow once it's posted 🙂
No problem Priya. Tomorrow is fine.
Uploaded the revised alto line for the Rutter. Bars 40 to 52 have changed, so please check your copy before Thursday rather than on the night.
Good. Thank you Tom. I'll print paper copies tomorrow for anyone who needs them.

note: 19:30-21:00 Tom and Ffion walk along the Taff, cold but dry

text: Ffion says the Rutter bars were written by someone who hated altos. I have told her that is unkind to Rutter.
Tom, you said that.
Fair.
Bar 44 is the one to watch. The tenors have it too, but nobody listens to us.
Go to bed.
Copies are printed. I'll bring them Thursday.
Ffion's on the 0745 so I'm the only one in this house awake. Coffee is terrible.

note: Tue 06:00-14:30 Owen on the 17 route, Cathays to Splott and back

text: Rota's out. I'm off Thursday so I can come. Sorry it took so long.
Good. Thank you Priya.
I can do Cathays on Thursday if you want the lift. About 6.
Thanks Owen. That would be good, if it's no trouble.
No trouble.
Welcome to the Rutter Priya. Bar 44 is yours now.
It isn't.
Found the original score in the library copy. The altos were printed in pencil in the margin, so possibly it was unkind after all.
Pencil in the margin isn't the same as unkind.
Which library copy. The cabinet or the one on the piano.
Cabinet. Second shelf, Rutter in the spine.
Thank you. I'll look Thursday.

note: Tue 21:40-23:30 Tom at the laptop doing a password reset for a dentist in Pontcanna, Ffion on the sofa with a book

text: Out early. Chairs Thursday, I'll be at the hall before six.
Good. Owen, there is a stack of Tom's copies on the piano if you want to check them before the rest of us.
They are not my copies. They are the library's copies. I have only been looking after them.
Yes, Tom.
Go to work.
I am work. Ffion is work too but she has a bus.
Dog has been sick on the hall rug at home. She is fine now. The rug is not.
Oh no. Hope she's ok.
She is ok. Eating biscuits again so I think she is recovered.
Rutter bar 44 has been discussed enough. Can we all agree the tenors have it worst
No.
I'll take the altos' side on that one, Tom. Bar 44 is hard.
Thank you Priya. Some support at last.

note: Wed 19:00-21:30 Owen at home in Roath, cooking, flatmates out

text: Does anyone have a spare folder. Mine has a coffee ring on the cover and I don't want it in my bag on Thursday.
I have one. I'll bring it.
Thank you Ffion.
Off shift. Bar 44 is practised. Badly, but practised.
